security_spec.violation_condition: On RV32 with Sspmpen enabled, if the kernel updates spmpen and spmpenh as two separate CSR writes without clearing SIE in sstatus (i.e., non-atomically with respect to interrupts), an interrupt delivered between the two writes observes a partially-updated spmpen mask, leaving SPMP in an inconsistent state where entries from both outgoing and incoming tasks are simultaneously active or OS-resident entries are momentarily disabled
security_spec.summary: Non-atomic spmpen/spmpenh update on RV32 leaves a window where interrupt handlers see inconsistent SPMP masks, enabling cross-task memory access

findings.finding: Sspmp extension is not implemented in this FreeBSD RISC-V source tree. No CSR definitions for spmpen (0x207), spmpenh (0x207 on RV32), spmpaddr*, or spmpcfg* exist. The CSR encoding header only defines standard S-mode CSRs (sstatus, sie, stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sip, satp) and M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, pmpcfg*, pmpaddr*). Without Sspmp support, there is no code that writes spmpen/spmpenh non-atomically with respect to interrupts, so the described vulnerability pattern cannot manifest.
Context switch path does not save/restore any SPMP-related CSRs because Sspmp is not enabled. No spmpen/spmpenh register access instructions exist in the context switch code.
findings.snippet: (no SPMP CSR references found in swtch.S)

findings.finding: bhyve hypervisor does not virtualize SPMP CSRs for guests because Sspmp is not implemented. The vmm code only handles hstatus, stvec, and senvcfg in the hypervisor context switch path.
findings.snippet: (no SPMP CSR references found in vmm code)

findings.finding: No csrw/csrc/csrs instructions targeting spmpen or spmpenh exist anywhere in the codebase. The vulnerability pattern (two separate CSR writes to spmpen and spmpenh without SIE cleared) cannot be triggered.

While the codebase is currently compliant because Sspmp is not implemented, any future PR adding Sspmp support must ensure that spmpen and spmpenh (on RV32) are updated atomically with respect to interrupts. The required pattern is: (1) clear SIE in sstatus, (2) write spmpen, (3) write spmpenh if RV32, (4) restore SIE. Alternatively, use a single CSRRS/CSRRC instruction if only modifying a subset of bits, or disable SPMP entirely during the update window. FreeBSD's intr_restore()/intr_disable() provide suitable wrappers for this purpose.
